=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:2647-2656,2717-2724 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_1-fast, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The bulk-delete guard does not pass the active threshold label/effective threshold to downstream steps, so the P3 issue comment and Telegram alert always say "bulk deletion exceeded BULK_DELETE_THRESHOLD" even when the markdown-only threshold fired.
  WHY: The guard computes the correct label for the inline error, but only outputs `bulk-delete` and the count, while the consumer hardcodes `BULK_DELETE_THRESHOLD`, making markdown-only blocks report the wrong threshold name.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:2651-2656,2717-2724,2753,2780 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The commit-guard step does not forward `threshold_label`/`effective_threshold`, so the downstream P3 handler always renders the bulk-delete message as `BULK_DELETE_THRESHOLD`.
  WHY: The inline error uses the computed threshold correctly, but the issue comment and Telegram alert are built from a hardcoded human-readable string, which is wrong when the markdown-only threshold is the one exceeded.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:2652-2655,2717-2723,2753,2780-2781 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The P3 failure handling maps `DCB_REASON=bulk-delete` to `bulk deletion exceeded BULK_DELETE_THRESHOLD` without knowing whether the markdown-only threshold was the one exceeded.
  WHY: The guard computes the active threshold correctly, but it is not emitted as an output, so the downstream comment and Telegram alert can contradict the actual rejected threshold.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:2648,2720-2724 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The downstream P3 failure handler hardcodes `BULK_DELETE_THRESHOLD` in the human-readable message even when the lenient markdown-only threshold was the one exceeded.
  WHY: This makes the GitHub issue comment and Telegram alert report the wrong threshold name, which is misleading during operator review.
=== END FINDINGS FROM moonshotai_kimi-k2_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:2647-2654,2722-2724 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The bulk-delete guard writes only `destructive_commit_blocked=bulk-delete` to `GITHUB_OUTPUT`, while the P3 step maps that reason to a fixed `BULK_DELETE_THRESHOLD` message.
  WHY: When the 100-file markdown cap is the actual violated threshold, the Telegram alert and issue comment incorrectly claim the 3-file threshold was exceeded.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===

=== FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_1-fast ===
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:~2615-2651,~2647-2648,2720-2724 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The post-guard outputs do not distinguish `BULK_DELETE_THRESHOLD` from `BULK_DELETE_THRESHOLD_MD`, so downstream consumers render a stale human-readable bulk-delete reason.
  WHY: The later alert/comment steps map `bulk-delete` to a hardcoded threshold name, which is misleading when the markdown-only cap triggered the block.
=== END FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_1-fast ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5 ===
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:2647-2652,2717-2724 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The guard emits `destructive_commit_blocked=bulk-delete` without the active threshold label, and the P3 case statement always turns that into `bulk deletion exceeded BULK_DELETE_THRESHOLD`.
  WHY: As a result, all-markdown deletions that hit the 100-file limit are reported as if they had hit the 3-file limit, which misleads operators.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5 ===
